hypothesis: Stocks in the highest quintile of residual momentum from trading days t-251 through t-20 outperform the lowest quintile over the following 20 trading days.
signal: Each daily stock return is decomposed into same-day PIT eligible-universe market return plus same-day PIT eligible sector excess return; residual = stock return - market - sector_excess. Score is cumulative residual return from t-251 through t-20; the most recent 20 sessions are excluded.
direction: High residual momentum (Q5) minus low residual momentum (Q1) is positive.
universe: PIT Sharadar domestic common stocks, price >= $1, trailing 63-session median dollar volume >= $500,000, >=252 sessions history; exclude Fama Financial Services, Real Estate, Healthcare.
formation_and_execution: Signal is formed with data through close t. Cross-sectional characterization uses close[t] to close[t+h] forward returns for h in 1,5,10,20. The costed long-only implementation forms at t close, enters next-session open, holds 20 sessions, and exits at open.
implementation: Top-quintile long, equal weight, rebalance every 20 trading days, 10bp round-trip cost under the standardized model. Weekly and 10-session turnover are diagnostic only.

classification.supported: primary 20-day Q5-Q1 HAC t >= 2.39, positive 20-day IC, and positive factor-adjusted spread alpha with no material implementation/orthogonality failure
classification.falsified: primary 20-day Q5-Q1 spread <= 0 with HAC t <= -1.0, or factor-adjusted alpha <= 0 with t <= -1.0

integrity.used_holdout_rule: Not evaluated by this program; results are development characterization only and cannot constitute fresh holdout validation.
